item.title: CVE Program Launches Frontier AI Researcher CNA Pilot
item.description: CVE Program Launches Frontier AI Researcher CNA PilotblogBy CVE Program|July 28, 2026Today, theCVE™ Programis launching theFrontier AI Researcher CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) Pilot, an initial six-month effort withAnthropicandOpenAI. This is a closed pilot, and participation is limited at this time to these two organizations. The pilot is intended to help the CVE Program evaluate how the large-scale, AI-enabled vulnerability research capabilities of frontier AI labs can contribute to accurate, coordinated, actionable, and sustainableCVE Records.Under the pilot, Anthropic and OpenAI may assignCVE Identifiers (CVE IDs)for vulnerabilities they discover in widely adopted products and applications when those products are not already within another CNA’sscope.

item.title: Anthropic Added as CVE Numbering Authority (CNA)
item.description: Anthropic Added as CVE Numbering Authority (CNA)newsJuly 28, 2026Anthropic, PBCis now aCVE Numbering Authority (CNA)for Vulnerabilities in software, services, and open-source projects developed, maintained, or distributed by Anthropic. This includes Claude Code, Claude Desktop, browser extensions, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) SDKs and reference servers, Anthropic API client SDKs, and related developer tooling published under the Anthropic, anthropic-experimental, and modelcontextprotocol GitHub organizations.In addition, Anthropic is participating in the CVE Program’sFrontier AI Researcher CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) Pilotunder the following “AI Researcher” scope: Vulnerabilities discovered by Anthropic that are not within another CNA’s scope.

item.title: Thank You for Attending theCVE and AI Vulnerability DiscoveryCommunity Event!
item.description: Thank You for Attending theCVE and AI Vulnerability DiscoveryCommunity Event!newsAugust 4, 2026TheCVE Programwould like to thank everyone who attended, or presented at, the free publicCVE in an Era of AI-Enabled Vulnerability Discoveryvirtual conference on July 30, 2026. Community participation was strong throughout the event, and all of the community presentations, panel discussions, and interactive sessions were highly informative and constructive. The conference video will be available soon on theCVE Program YouTube Channel.

item.title: Haverford Systems Added as CVE Numbering Authority (CNA)
item.description: Haverford Systems Added as CVE Numbering Authority (CNA)newsAugust 4, 2026Haverford Systems, Inc.is now aCVE Numbering Authority (CNA)for all products for Haverford Systems brands, PTZOptics and HuddleCamHD (supported products and end-of-life/end-of-service products), as well as vulnerabilities in third-party software discovered by Haverford Systems that are not in another CNA’s scope.

item.title: NATO Cyber Security Centre Added as CVE Numbering Authority (CNA)
item.description: NATO Cyber Security Centre Added as CVE Numbering Authority (CNA)newsAugust 4, 2026NATO Cyber Security Centreis now aCVE Numbering Authority (CNA)for vulnerabilities in commercial off-the-shelf software (COTS) selected for inclusion in the NATO Approved Software List (A2SL) that are not in the scope of another CNA.

item.title: Postiz Added as CVE Numbering Authority (CNA)
item.description: Postiz Added as CVE Numbering Authority (CNA)newsAugust 4, 2026Postizis now aCVE Numbering Authority (CNA)for Postiz products and projects only including: the core repository for postiz-app (github.com/gitroomhq/postiz-app); all gitroomhq repositories that are official components, tooling, or integrations of Postiz; official Postiz container images published under gitroomhq on GHCR; official Postiz CLI tools and NPM packages (NPM org: @postiz); Postiz-Cloud related infrastructure and services. (API, Frontend, Configurations etc.); and plugins for Postiz maintained within the gitroomhq organization.

item.title: Video from “CVE and AI Vulnerability Discovery” Virtual Conference Now Available
item.description: Video from “CVE and AI Vulnerability Discovery” Virtual Conference Now AvailableblogBy CVE Program|August 12, 2026TheCVE™ Programhosted a free public virtual conference, “CVE in an Era of AI-Enabled Vulnerability Discovery,” on July 30, 2026, about how AI-enabled vulnerability discovery is affecting the CVE Program and the broader vulnerability management ecosystem — and where current models may need to adapt. Theconference videois now available on theCVE Program Channel on YouTube.
